title: Line Take Match
user: Indie animators and game creators recording character lines who need to compare takes for level, pace, and emotional consistency without cloning anyone’s voice.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An animator reports inconsistent, flat AI voice results and expensive unusable human takes across roughly 40 lines, and asks for a better workflow.
A puzzle-game developer says stream-level volume control is missing, making audio implementation and iteration tedious; the request has 18 reactions.

recurrence: Two independent production problems across 2025–26: iterating audio assets and keeping many dialogue lines usable, rather than merely generating more speech.
current_workaround: Keep naming conventions and notes, compare waveforms in a DAW, normalize manually, then discover level or pace mismatches in the edit.
incumbents_and_gap: Audacity and DAWs edit audio; ElevenLabs and other generators create voices. The gap is a consent-safe, local takeboard specifically for comparing delivery against a chosen reference line, not generating or impersonating a voice.
smallest_useful_product: A local web app that imports creator-owned WAV/MP3 takes, groups them by line, shows loudness, duration, pause, and pitch-range comparison against a selected approved take, and exports a handoff CSV.
success_measure: A creator labels and compares 40 lines in under 30 minutes and flags at least five materially inconsistent takes before export.
constraints: Process audio locally; obtain performer consent for all material; present measurements as review cues rather than quality scores; respect licensed-music and performer-rights boundaries.
why_distinct: It improves human creative direction and take selection without being a thin generative-voice wrapper.
